question.text: Tanjore Capital (corporate investor in a Cat I AIF) earns exempt buyback income of INR 5 crore in FY25 (buyback on 20 September 2024 - before the 1 October 2024 cutover). Tanjore had booked INR 40 lakh of management-level expenses partially attributable to this exempt stream. From the LP's tax perspective, which provision disallows expenses attributable to exempt income?

answer.text: Section 14A read with Rule 8D - expenditure in relation to exempt income is not deductible

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 460 and 475-477), Section 14A read with Rule 8D disallows expenditure incurred in relation to income that does not form part of total income. A buyback completed on or before 30 September 2024 was exempt in the shareholder's hands under Section 10(34A), so related expenses are disallowable under Section 14A. Rule 8D prescribes the formulaic disallowance. Buybacks on or after 1 October 2024 are taxable in the shareholder's hands and no longer attract Section 14A on the same logic. The Trap: Option A - Section 80M is the inter-corporate dividend deduction; opposite effect. Option C - Section 56(2)(x) applies to below-FMV receipts, not to exempt income. Option D - treaty override under Section 90(2) is unrelated to expense disallowance. Note: The 20 September 2024 buyback date falls in FY 2024-25; the stem label has been corrected to FY25 to match the pre-1 October 2024 cutover wording in pages 464 and 475-477.
